provenance.interpretation: Counter deltas are modulo-256 correlations; they are never labelled transaction counts.

alternative_models.distinguishing_prediction: Delta scales with requested/processed element count rather than number of API invocations.
alternative_models.evidence_against_or_for: Fully processed batches imply a transaction count equal to element count.

alternative_models.distinguishing_prediction: Each invocation increments counter once, independent of item-array length.
alternative_models.evidence_against_or_for: Delta should be 1 for all batch sizes.

alternative_models.distinguishing_prediction: Only successfully processed slots advance counter; failed element slots do not.
alternative_models.evidence_against_or_for: Deltas track processed elements, diverging when item errors occur.

alternative_models.model: One transaction per invocation plus processed elements
alternative_models.distinguishing_prediction: An invocation contributes one, plus each processed element.
alternative_models.evidence_against_or_for: Delta should be 1 + processed elements per call.

alternative_models.model: One transaction per batch with variable-sized server work
alternative_models.distinguishing_prediction: Counter records a server work unit that might depend on cache, item type, duplicate/cyclic inputs, or request size.
alternative_models.evidence_against_or_for: Repeatable item/order/cache contrasts or non-linear deltas distinguish it.

alternative_models.model: Counter is an unrelated modulo-256 event stream
alternative_models.distinguishing_prediction: Observed correlation can arise from another event source; delta is not transaction count evidence.
alternative_models.evidence_against_or_for: Would not consistently track intervening known calls in independently varied trials.
